verdict.tagline: Grand medieval battles suffer from fragile mods and shallow management.
for_you_if: you want large-scale medieval tactical battles
not_for_you_if: you rely heavily on community mods for your campaigns
you want deep political and clan management systems
you expect game updates that do not break your setup

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the early game is difficult and challenging to progress through financially.

citations.review_text: i fel like it's just too difficult to make money early game, too few sidequests/jobs, it doesn't make sense that your main source of income is selling junk you get from looters, if you try to make money with trade, you can get a 100% markup on the merchandise, but your net profit will be -15%~-30% still bc you need troops to be safe on the road.. i was very underwhelmed by this game, it gives you the feeling of a open map, free roam, do wtv you want, roleplaying game, but it actually puts strong guardrails on what you're supposed to do by having unbalanced mechanics, big disappointment

Saw the game on sale and finally got it after it was sitting in my wishlist for a year or two, the start of this game is pretty hard but it gets easier as you progress, i love this game but for others its either you really like it or you dont, so if you like conquering medeival worlds and commanding armies, this game is for you, and honestly this game is one of those games where you make a ton of progress and lose it all just because the enemy has better troops and you leave for a few months but you will always come back.(If you actually like it)
Btw this is one of my first ever strategy games i played, i tried total war before and i hated it, but i actually like this game.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Mid-game campaigns reveal shallow management systems and unhelpful artificial intelligence.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the campaign and clan management systems lack depth and control, making AI clan groups unhelpful in managing territories or avoiding poor battles.

citations.review_text:
[h3]I'm M&B fan since my friend sent me demo of the first game through Gadu-Gadu messenger. tldr; This game is terrible, just go and play Warhammer Total War 3 already with TPP mod as it does everything that Bannerlord does but just better.[/h3]

I'm at 25 hours, at the point of the game when you have city/castle/settlement already and need deeper management as you are not fighting 50vs50 with your party anymore. 

Your clan groups are completely useless, everything they do is gathering recruits, spending your money and then participating in lost battles all the time and getting captured by enemy. They just can go with their whole army and help some lord that can't just win. [u]YOU HAVE NO CONTROL OVER THEM[/u]! As you can't give order to stay in the castle or avoid dangerous parts of the map. 

Battlefield AI also doesn't exist, in 1500vs1500 battle you can make perfect flank making huge chaos and disruption (for example catching enemy bowmans), but other allies will just stand and wait letting enemy infantry to turn back, move back to you, and get rid of you and even return to formation back.

Campaign AI suck, for around 20 years I sit in endless war as Swadia vs Sturgia and Cesar. Enemy lords spam war surrender immidiately while only they can, meanwhile my kingdom lords decline all peace treaties for no reason, it lead to situation that ally lords AI can't split army properly fighting double war on that scale and they loss territories (cities, castles) despite of that we have advantage. King can't force peace treaty and meanwhile he force all new castles to me :|

In a game with [u]Mount & Blade[/u] title, cavalry is just pointless, as they charge, miss with hit with their lance, retreat and charge again. If terrain isn't flat they block on hills and objects and became completely useless. Ordering your cavalry to get off mount and fight against other cavalry meele even in open field works much much better which is a joke.

Infantry troops are difficult to train,…

In reality, I’ve played much more than my recorded hours suggest, and I certainly have a few things to say about the game.

- The bots are still just as dim-witted, and the diplomacy remains clunky. I expected improvements after four years, but it seems the developers have their own reasons for leaving these issues unaddressed. It feels like a recurring trait of the entire series.

- The economy is broken. The core loop for making money—market trading, fighting, selling captives, and ransoming hostages—is still the only reliable way to get ahead. It’s disappointing, especially since you can tell they tried to implement other systems; for instance, workshops and caravans still fail to generate the kind of income you’d expect.

- The clan system is bizarre. You can’t completely wipe out an enemy clan, and your own clan can’t be wiped out either. What’s the point of having a family if it takes 20 years for a child to actually become useful? There’s no option for polygamy to bypass companion limits, nor is there any meaningful way to establish sub-clans—it’s a feature that exists just for the sake of existing.

- War declarations feel completely random. A losing faction will repeatedly declare war on a much stronger opponent, and the council refuses to make peace—even after suffering massive losses in both men and resources. Furthermore, there’s a total reluctance to form alliances or trade agreements; 99% of the time, those options are simply unavailable.

On the bright side, the battles remain excellent—and the sieges, whether you’re attacking or defending, are a huge plus.

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term play brings constant mod breakage, erratic artificial intelligence, and fading multiplayer populations.

claims.claim: Game updates frequently break installed mods, rendering them incompatible or causing the game to stop working.

citations.review_text: I genuinely enjoy this game. It's got a wonderful community, lots of great mods, and feels much better to play than Warband. However, it suffers (and has suffered, for years) from a development process that is glacial at the best of times, and a profound lack of support & communication. Recently the modding community has been pretty much put indefinitely on hold by the combination of a new manual approval process for the workshop (Which seems like it was imposed upon Talesworlds, I genuinely don't mind) and a new update for the game making everything incompatible. Normally this wouldn't be much of an issue, but manual approvals are just.. not happening. At all. It's been weeks. Multiplayer communities using any sort of mods simply cannot operate and there seems to be no end in sight because Talesworlds has seemingly no willingness to take action to resolve this relatively simple, easy to fix problem. It's infuriating, needless, and just another exhausting example of how the Mount and Blade community is so often left out to dry.
Unplayable without mods, and every update breaks mods.
I am tired of this game, started again in autumn 2026, installed collection of mods and another update happened, game stopped workng again, guys seriously, f..off

Minimal support for mod developers. Taleworlds locked their workshop because ai slop mods were giving people viruses, and then refused to approve any multiplayer mods. To top it all off they drop an update (which breaks basically every mod) in the midst of the workshop lockdown, effectively killing every multiplayer event. Then they refuse to give any sort of clarity on what they’re doing, giving only vague “we’re aware and working on it” responses, when in actuality the entire studio is jerking off doing nothing

Guess it doesn’t matter since they’ve already gotten our money!

However, it suffers (and has suffered, for years) from a development process that is glacial at the best of times, and a profound lack of support & communication. It's infuriating, needless, and just another exhausting example of how the Mount and Blade community is so often left out to dry.

Taleworlds has effectively left the multiplayer community in the dark with their recent lack of communication over mod approvals. Several multiplayer events have disbanded over it and their multiplayer community, literally held together by the people who willingly devote their time to organizing these mass events through their mods, is dying by the day. They continuously post vague updates about their "process" but do not provide any real information or timelines for approval. Moving to Nexus is also not an option as any barrier to entry to an event reduces it's population by over half, we saw this with bloodhold. Adding the requirement to use nexus killed their event overnight. The multiplayer scene may never recover as people move on due to their lack of any sort of communication or initiative to approve mods. It would be easy for them to approve minor updates before events to keep these communities, that keep the multiplayer scene of their game relevant, alive and engaged. Complete fumbling of how to engage with your community. Should be studied as ways to kill your MP community overnight.

TaleWorlds has broken the workshop by refusing to let modders release updates without approval - is not approving updates for upwards of 3-to-4 weeks - and then releases a server update which requires modders to update to maintain compatibility. Incredibly shortsighted it's like they're actively trying to kill multiplayer. Since War Sails they've caused a bunch of unintended bugs with MP and they took months to fix some basic ones like holding alt to highlight was not working for months, other things too.

One of the greatest examples of a games combat system setting itself apart from its peers. I've been a fan of the Mount and Blade series for years now and I can safely say I've not played anything truly like it in my time gaming. The single player offers a unique experience of building ones army and kingdom up, while the multiplayer has caused me to sink thousands of hours into it across the series.

However that is not why I am leaving this negative review, as it stands Talewords has effectively killed the modding scene by implementing a system they have put little effort in to currently. Workshop mods need to be manually approved by decision from the team and as of this current moment, precious few have been approved, if any at all. This would be absurd for any game, but the Mount and Blade devs should know better, considering their previous title, Warband, has been carried by its modding scene to this very day. You could look through Warband mods and come across several that are well worth time sunk into them. Yet through lack of support and neglect, Bannerlord modding has slowed to a crawl over the years, while this seems to be the final nail for many modders I am in contact with.

This has killed the MP community and severely impacted the SP community. I love this game, but as the years go on, it's become apparent I love it far more than the developers ever could. In its current state, I can not recommend picking up this game and I implore the developers to do better.

citations.review_text:
这是一款优点和缺点都非常明显的游戏。但绝对值得购买。
先说缺点：1.无法使用摇杆畅快游玩，多数时候还给依赖键盘鼠标。绝对的缺点。2. 人物是真丑啊。无论是随机生成的NPC还是玩家的角色，都是只有丑和更丑的区别。其实只要开发者愿意，简单调整一下程序数值，是完全可以生成正常模样的人物的。还是审美趣味的问题。3. 战斗动作设计是相当的落后，就算是用多年以前的标准来衡量，都是算差的，偏偏游戏还有大量的动作成分， 战场冲杀，竞技场搏斗手感都不好。最差的是那极端幼稚粗糙的潜行暗杀模式，应该直接删除，集中精力做自己擅长的内容。
再说优点，这游戏最大的亮点甚至是神奇的地方就是以极低的硬件要求实现了玩家带领千军万马冲杀搏击，指挥若定，百万军中取上将首级的英雄梦。现场代入感非常高。值得每一个曾有过英雄梦的玩家入手。就这一条优点盖过了它所有的缺点。
8/10 the game has amazing depth. the only issue is the combat system is a little janky and outdated. the best feature is the massive amount of mods for this game.

A great potential absolutely ruined by a terrible company.

Why?

Horrible combat animations, slightly better graphics than warband (which is honestly a better game) AND despite being way older than Bannerlord, Warband has believe it or not more PVP mechanics than Bannerlord. You might know what I am talking about if you have 3000+ hours in Warband multi.

Terrible for modders and modding due to a shit ass engine which breaks the game easily even with a few QOL mods. I am starting to think that devs purposefully made this game to near-impossible to mod.

Lack of content in Vanilla game, horrible circle-jerking multiplayer community and single player campaign AI

Again, lack of content. The new DLC could've been added as an update instead of a DLC. It only adds naval combat and a new faction (which is actually in Warband already) along with some tweaks to the map.

Horrible AI, you tell your inf to make a shieldwall, then advance towards the enemy group, only for them to form a moshpit while breaking the formation. The only difference between elite troops and looters is that elite troops have better armor and stats, the way they fight is absolutely the same.

Non-existent Diplomacy. Wars have no consequence whatsoever. You can repeatedly beat an enemy kingdom, take most of their fiefs, and yet they still comeback days after with replenished troops and numbers. Like dude, I capture and behead your King, how the fuck you are still fighting a war against me??

This game was first announced back in 2012, OG Warbanders will remember. And the game came out in 2020. Are you telling me that Taleworlds did all these in 8 years? If you ask me, that is a huge fucking disappointment.

I will tell you my own piece of mind about why this game is at this stage, is horrendous.

Lack of competition. There are no games like Bannerlord in the market at the moment, so these guys are just sitting in their office all day and eat kebab while doing absolutely fuckall. Wi…

claims.claim: The early game is punishing and difficult for new players, with unarmored looters posing a severe threat to beginners.

citations.review_text:
Smart game. Bannerlord’s systems encourage the player to create their own company of advisors and warriors, and rewards them greatly for doing so. Their character sheets start specialized toward a few different areas, but it’s up to you on how you want to build them. Companions can do so many things here: form their own wandering army to scope out the area and wipe out enemies, do quests for the player to cut down on busywork, and even participate in arranged, political marriages in a few select cases. The social systems are the biggest improvement from Warband, and by the midpoint of the game you’ll have woven a web of allies and foes alike — the world really feels alive! Factions are constantly fighting one another, alliances will shift, and the people you surround yourself with one day may become your enemies next week. Even so, the game’s influence system helps a lot with coordinating strikes, and I felt appropriately powerful by the game’s final hours.

That’s not to say that getting there is easy. Bannerlord’s early game is much more unforgiving than Warband’s, and I’m not entirely sure if I’m a fan of it. Even if you pick the prologue options that make you stronger in combat, a shirtless looter with a rusty knife is gonna fold you into a pretzel if you aren’t careful. And I do love that combat: reaction speed is everything. Knowing whether to block or stab can be the difference between life or death, and the player’s fragility is especially heightened in the early game. One benefit of this ruthlessness is that running low level quests for EXP becomes a necessity. Stopping poachers, working the fields… You don’t become a legend overnight, and the game stresses that appropriately. You’ll have to count your coins and keep an eye on that spending, and maintaining supplies is a big deal early on.

This all builds up to the late game, where you’ll have allied yourself to a kingdom or created one of your own. It’s my favorite part of the game, and it forces the play…
Fun but not well balanced for early gameplay.
First time playing warband got stomped by looters/bandits, and then first time playing bannerlord still getting stomped by looters. 10/10!

Bannerlord is not a game for everyone. At the beginning it can be overwhelming and difficult to understand, despite the campaign having an introduction to the game mechanics. In some ways, it's a bit rough, but it knows how to be entertaining.

If you manage to overcome this first impact, what comes next is a game that, combined with mod support, will give you hundreds of hours of playtime.

citations.review_text: so I really have a love hate relationship with this game. I do love the aspect of a campaign and story  to follow. but the way I play games is having a goal that goal useally being a specific acheivment. but this game is not very multiplayer popular to my knowledge sat in queue for over an hour at some point. and still haven't found a single multiplayer experience. yet some of the achievments is locked on to multiplayer. another issue I have is the sailing. the only reason is most of the important things is on land. ship combat is one of my favourite things in combast. so it really bothers me it feels so useless. that said. Nothing more joyful than the combat, having 100 archers 100 horse archers and 100 huscarl and 200 calvery, the sounds when everything is just happening is like drugs tbh, it hits hard, I genuinly enjoy the rest of this game, one thing it does well is the speed of the game. every step of the game takes about the same amouint of time to progress depending on a few variants but you get to exerpeince the horror of running away from 30 bandits to the joy of sieging a castle with 3000 men and everything in between. so as said love hate relationship.

My honest opinion, this game is amazing, but it only has so much replayability before it starts getting bland, repetitive and boring. Idk the game plan that the devs have in mind, but if they intend on adding content and sprucing up the game they need to do it asap. Multiplayer is dead, unless its custom matches or player ran servers. Awesome game i definitely recommend, but lets be real, itll only keep your attention for so long before it sits in your steam library for a few months until a decent update or addon is added.

claims.claim: Game updates routinely break existing mods.

citations.review_text: I genuinely enjoy this game. It's got a wonderful community, lots of great mods, and feels much better to play than Warband. However, it suffers (and has suffered, for years) from a development process that is glacial at the best of times, and a profound lack of support & communication. Recently the modding community has been pretty much put indefinitely on hold by the combination of a new manual approval process for the workshop (Which seems like it was imposed upon Talesworlds, I genuinely don't mind) and a new update for the game making everything incompatible. Normally this wouldn't be much of an issue, but manual approvals are just.. not happening. At all. It's been weeks. Multiplayer communities using any sort of mods simply cannot operate and there seems to be no end in sight because Talesworlds has seemingly no willingness to take action to resolve this relatively simple, easy to fix problem. It's infuriating, needless, and just another exhausting example of how the Mount and Blade community is so often left out to dry.
Unplayable without mods, and every update breaks mods.
I am tired of this game, started again in autumn 2026, installed collection of mods and another update happened, game stopped workng again, guys seriously, f..off

single_points.text: One reviewer says that a target is painted on your back as soon as you acquire the big mcguffin.

citation.review_text:
So many years later and the devs are still peddling this game with a completely masochistic storyline, one that ALL the achievements are tied into.

I get that this game is set at the time this universe's Roman Empire fell, but it's a joke that you get a target painted on your back as soon as you acquire the big mcguffin. This BS wasn't in Warband, and it shouldn't have been in this game.

Add on the fact that the campaign AI is a joke when it comes to diplomacy, map movement, and engaging enemies (I watched two armies that had numerical superiority over a besieging enemy  when my army was factored in just sit there until I engaged, then the map mechanics made it so that only my army was fighting, AT A 2 TO 1 DISADVANTAGE.

Only get this game if you want to play sandbox, the storyline is a complete joke that'll cause you to waste several hours of your life.
